other_side: Where NLW argues the market's relentless bubble-hunting is a pressure-release valve, that circular financing is nothing like the dot-com trap because OpenAI pays cash for GPUs, and that cancelled data centres reflect hard construction rather than weak demand, Zitron's argument is the mirror image. He contends the AI build-out is a genuine debt-funded asset bubble whose special-purpose vehicles are the equivalent of 2008's collateralised debt obligations: off-balance-sheet structures, reminiscent of Enron, that hide something like 1.65 trillion dollars of obligations while NVIDIA finances the very companies buying its chips and then rents that capacity back. He estimates that 70 to 90 percent of compute demand comes from OpenAI and Anthropic, two loss-making firms, and that roughly fifteen times more data-centre capacity is being built than real demand supports. On his reading the freakouts are not preventing a bubble; they are belatedly noticing a real one.
truth_beneath: The single variable both men orbit is whether demand for AI compute is real and durable enough to service the debt now being raised against it. Both accept the facts of scale: staggering capital spending heading past a trillion dollars, roughly half the S&P 500 AI-exposed, and much of the financing routed through hyperscalers and neoclouds. The empirical question that will resolve is whether paying customers exist beyond OpenAI and Anthropic to fill the capacity, and whether those two can keep paying. The observable that settles it is third-party compute revenue and remaining performance obligations from buyers who are not hyperscalers or the two big labs, plus whether the data-centre SPVs actually meet their debt-service ratios once leases begin. The residue is worldview: NLW reads compulsive bubble-calling as self-correcting; Zitron reads it as recognition of hidden systemic leverage. NLW is vindicated if diverse enterprise demand climbs to absorb the build and spending keeps being funded without defaults; Zitron if demand stays concentrated in two unprofitable labs and the SPVs start missing payments. Both are polemicists with incentives, NLW bullish and anti-doom, Zitron bubble-certain and anti-hype, so the signal is where they agree despite opposite priors: both concede the spending is enormous and both concede it currently hinges on two loss-making companies. Watch whether compute revenue from anyone other than OpenAI, Anthropic and their hyperscaler backers actually materialises.
